cutscene.title: The Glass Awakens
cutscene.style: Low, slow push across a mirror-black plain toward a single trembling gold horizon; quiet and vast

captions.text: Something far away has begun to wake.

notes: A slow low push-in over the black glass toward the trembling gold thread, ending at the Wanderer's view.

thought: The glass hums and pulses in answer to the light. Maybe the light is calling me, or the floor is alive. The orange flecks scattered across the glass look like a trail.
action: Kneel and press my palm to the glass. What is the humming, and are the amber flecks forming a pattern leading toward the light?

ruling: The Wanderer kneels and presses a palm to the glass. Roll 8 is a partial: the humming resolves into a slow heartbeat-like rhythm that answers the light, and the amber flecks do form a curving trail toward the north. Touching it costs something: the glass drinks a little warmth and leaves a faint amber handprint that glows under the palm. A first mechanic is born, Resonance, as the Wanderer feels attuned to the pulse. Convey that the floor is alive and listening, and that the pulse quickens when the Wanderer faces the light.
announce: Resonance awakens: 1/10 — the glass knows your touch

roll.presentation: A heartbeat count: the pulse in the glass is counted against the Wanderer's own pulse.
roll.reason: Can the Wanderer understand the glass's hum without it taking something in return?

ops.label: Resonance
ops.rules: Rises when the Wanderer listens to, touches or follows the glass's pulse. Spent to wake dormant glass or read its trail. Higher values make the light answer.

objectives.text: Follow the amber trail north toward the light

narration: You kneel, and the glass is cool as deep water under your palm. The humming sharpens into a slow rhythm, a heartbeat far larger than yours, and it is answering the light on the horizon. Where your hand rests, the glass drinks a little of your warmth and leaves a handprint of glowing amber. Around you the scattered flecks seem to stir and draw together into a long, curving trail that runs north toward the gold. When you lift your eyes to the light, the pulse quickens, and you understand that the floor is alive and has been listening for you.

facts.description: A softly glowing amber handprint about 20 cm long, set into the surface of the black glass where the Wanderer pressed a palm. Warm light pulses within it slowly, in time with the heartbeat of the glass.
facts.placement: At ground level directly beneath the Wanderer's position, at [0,0,0].

facts.description: A curving trail of amber flecks and hairline veins gathered into a bright ribbon about 30 cm wide, glowing just beneath the glass surface. It sweeps in a long gentle S-curve and brightens in slow pulses traveling northward.
facts.placement: Starts at amber_handprint and runs roughly 40 m north, bending slightly east then west, continuing toward golden_horizon_light.

facts.description: An endless flat plain of polished black volcanic glass, mirror-smooth, with hairline veins of amber light beneath the surface. It pulses with a slow heartbeat rhythm that quickens when the Wanderer faces north, and faint ripples of light spread outward with each beat.
facts.placement: Extends in all directions from the Wanderer at ground level, centered at [0,0,0].

notes: I pressed a glowing amber handprint into the glass under the Wanderer. From it, a pulsing amber ribbon winds in an S-curve 40 m north toward the light.

Remove or hide whatever causes the two white blobs near the Wanderer (the soft bloom puddles at roughly [0,0,2] and [3,0,4]). cutscene.style: Slow descending crane from a high, wide view of the glass plain to the Wanderer's eye line; amber handprint pulsing like a heartbeat, quiet and intimate

captions.text: Something vast has felt your hand.

notes: A slow crane-down from above the kneeling Wanderer to the handprint's amber glow, settling at the view that opens the next turn, with the trail running north toward the light.

thought: A bright trail winds north to a glowing figure by the horizon. Is it another wanderer, or the light itself? I should follow the trail.
action: Follow the glowing trail north, step by step, toward the luminous figure standing on the horizon.

ruling: Following the trail is safe, so no roll is needed. As the Wanderer walks, each footstep wakes a pulse in the glass and Resonance rises by 2. Halfway along, the glowing figure on the horizon resolves as a tall silhouette of light that does not move but seems to turn toward the Wanderer. Convey that the trail brightens underfoot, the heartbeat syncs with the Wanderer's steps, and the figure feels both like a person and like the light itself. A new clock, The Opening Eye, is born: the figure's attention is gathering, and it fills as the Wanderer nears.

narration: You walk, and the trail wakes beneath each step. Every boot-fall sends a ring of amber through the glass, and by the tenth stride the great heartbeat has fallen into step with yours. The ribbon brightens ahead of you as if it were being poured. Halfway along its curve, the light on the horizon gathers itself upward into a tall silhouette, narrow and unmoving, and it turns toward you without moving at all. It feels like a person, and it feels like the light itself wearing the shape of one. The glass hums low and warm, and you sense an attention gathering, like an eyelid slowly lifting.

cutscene.title: The Opening Eye
cutscene.style: Glass-level tracking through footfall rings, then a rising reveal where the horizon light stands and turns; amber on black, heartbeat rhythm, bloom swelling as an eyelid lifts

breakthrough: A rare alignment: the world itself leans in to watch.
notes: The Wanderer's footsteps wake the glass from a ground-level view of amber rings, then the camera rises to reveal the horizon light standing up as a silhouette that turns to watch.

assessment: Two turns in, this is a clean, single-image story: black glass, one warm thread of light, a trail that wakes underfoot, a figure that turns without moving. The visuals have improved sharply from the grey pixel-confetti slab of turn 0 to a genuinely dark mirror with readable veins and rings at turn 2, and the horizon column is a strong focal point. But with only one turn left, the story has set up a meeting it hasn't paid off, the figure is still 1.8 km away at the end of a 40 m trail, and the glitch-looking white blobs that the Designer has flagged three times are still in the overview. Turn 3 has to be the ending: the Eye opens, the figure meets the Wanderer, and we learn why the glass was listening.
narrative: Turn 3 is the finale, so resolve, don't tease. Collapse the distance: the figure either steps down from the horizon to stand at the trail's end, or the glass carries the Wanderer across (the heartbeat quickening into one long pulse). Answer the opening line "you arrive without remembering how": the figure should give back one concrete memory or name, or reveal that the Wanderer is what it was listening for (a reflection, a prior self, the last warmth it remembers). Fill the Opening Eye clock and end on a clear final image, not another "attention gathering" beat; we've had that twice.
visual: The biggest win is the encounter itself: get the 3 m figure within 10 m of the Wanderer so we finally see its gradient body, motes and reflection at human scale instead of a merged sun-column. Kill the white blobs for good; two are still visible in the overview and one at lower right in turn 2, and they read as bugs. Keep the Wanderer from blowing out (turn 1 was a white smear); the figure should be the only hot-core element. For the finale, let the sky shift cold-to-warm as the eye opens, and let the veins across the whole plain light up at once, so the ending reads as the plain waking.
builder: Fix the placement contradiction: amber_trail runs 40 m north but luminous_figure sits 1.8 km away "at the end of amber_trail." In turn 3, place the figure at the trail's actual end so the camera can frame both characters. Find and remove whatever produces the two soft white discs on the floor (likely leftover sprite halos or light-spot planes); the Designer has asked three times. Spend the remaining bytes on the figure's close-up form and a plain-wide vein flash, and drop the far horizon thread's redundant glow once the figure has moved close.
wanderer: This is the last turn: walk the rest of the way and arrive. Ask the figure direct questions: who are you, why were you listening for me, how did I get here, what does the handprint mean. Touch it or offer the glowing hand; spend Resonance to make the light answer rather than just approach it. Ask for a name, not a feeling.
experience: Game Master: Resonance 3/10 and the Eye at 1/4 cannot fill naturally in one turn, so make turn 3 a decisive spend: let the Wanderer burn Resonance to call the figure down and jump the clock to 4/4 with a single roll that decides the tone of the meeting (warm recognition vs. cold claim), and close the quest. Cutscene Director: turn 2 already got the eyelid-lift; the finale needs a different grammar, a static two-shot at glass level with the Wanderer and the 3 m figure both in frame, reflections meeting in the mirror, then one slow pull up as the whole plain's veins ignite. Narrator messages are lovely but are starting to repeat "heartbeat," "eyelid," and "attention"; vary the language for the ending.
breakthrough: Turn 3 is the final turn of the story and the first face-to-face meeting with the luminous figure, with the Opening Eye clock filling; the closing cutscene should be the climax.

thought: The light is close now and shaped like a person. I want a name from it, not just a feeling, and I'll offer my glowing hand.
action: Hold out my amber-marked hand and walk the last steps. "Who are you, and why were you listening for me? Tell me your name."

ruling: The Wanderer spends Resonance to call the figure down. Roll 9 plus a +1 modifier for the lit handprint and the earned trail gives 10, a hit: the meeting is warm recognition. The distance folds away and the figure stands before the Wanderer at the trail's end, bending to their height. Its answer is concrete. Its name is "Ember", and it is the last warmth the glass remembers, kept from whoever first came here. The warmth the glass drank at the handprint was an offering, and the figure says the Wanderer is what it was listening for: the one who returns. It gives back a single memory, a hand held out in the dark long ago, which matches the Wanderer's amber palm. Resonance drops by 3 to 0 as it is spent, and The Opening Eye fills to 4/4. Close the quest. End on a still image: the Wanderer's reflection and the figure's meet in the black mirror, and the plain's veins ignite in gold to the horizon. Use fresh language and avoid 'heartbeat', 'eyelid' and 'attention'.
announce: The Opening Eye is full: 4/4. Quest complete: The Waking Light.

breakthrough: Finale: the figure gives its name and reveals the Wanderer is the one it was waiting for.

narration: You lift your amber palm, and the trail ahead floods white-gold. The distance folds like cloth: the horizon slides toward you, and the tall figure is simply there, bending until its faceless head is level with yours. "Ember," it says, in a voice like warm air over cooling stone. "I am the last warmth this glass remembers. What you gave it at the handprint was an offering, and I have been listening for you, the one who returns." It lays a memory in your mind: a hand held out in the dark, long ago, the same size as yours. Your reflection rises in the black mirror to meet its own, and the veins ignite in gold to the edge of the world.

Don't exceed the 8 KB content budget: trim comments and shorten variable names.

export function build(T,p,c){const g=new T.Group(),B=(o,v,l)=>new T.MeshBasicMaterial({color:l||'#fff3cf',vertexColors:!!v,blending:T.AdditiveBlending,transparent:true,opacity:o,depthWrite:false,fog:false,toneMapped:false}),a=new T.Color('#ffb347'),b=new T.Color('#fff3cf'),k=new T.Color(),M=(G,m,y,s)=>{const e=new T.Mesh(G,m);e.position.y=y;if(s)e.scale.y=-1;g.add(e);return e};const bd=new T.CylinderGeometry(.25,.4,2.4,12),P=bd.attributes.position,C=[];for(let i=0;i<P.count;i++){k.lerpColors(a,b,(P.getY(i)+1.2)/2.4);C.push(k.r,k.g,k.b)}bd.setAttribute('color',new T.Float32BufferAttribute(C,3));const h=new T.SphereGeometry(.22,12,8);M(bd,B(.95,1),1.2);M(bd,B(.35,1),-1.2,1);M(h,B(.95),2.7);M(h,B(.35),-2.7,1);M(new T.CylinderGeometry(.35,.5,3.4,12),B(.08),1.7);const q=[];for(let i=0;i<40;i++)q.push(c.pick([-1,1])*c.range(.2,.5),c.range(0,3),c.range(-.2,.2));const pg=new T.BufferGeometry();pg.setAttribute('position',new T.Float32BufferAttribute(q,3));const pt=new T.Points(pg,new T.PointsMaterial({color:'#ffd98a',size:.15,transparent:true,depthWrite:false,blending:T.AdditiveBlending,fog:false}));g.add(pt);g.userData.p=pt;const r=M(new T.RingGeometry(1.4,1.5,48),B(.8,0,'#ffd98a'),.04);r.rotation.x=-Math.PI/2;return g}
export function update(o,t){const a=o.userData.p.geometry.attributes.position;for(let i=0;i<a.count;i++)a.setY(i,(a.getY(i)+.004)%3);a.needsUpdate=true}

ops.name: amber_ripple
ops.doc: expanding amber ring; params: max (m)
ops.code:
export function build(T,p,c){const m=new T.MeshBasicMaterial({color:'#ffb347',blending:T.AdditiveBlending,transparent:true,opacity:0,depthWrite:false,toneMapped:false}),r=new T.Mesh(new T.RingGeometry(.9,1,64),m);r.rotation.x=-Math.PI/2;r.position.y=.02;const g=new T.Group();g.add(r);g.userData={m,r};return g}
export function update(o,t,d,p){const k=(t%2.5)/2.5,s=.2+k*((p.max||6)-.2);o.userData.r.scale.set(s,s,s);o.userData.m.opacity=.35*(1-k)}
